## As R.E.M. ascended from scrappy college rock beginnings to arenas, they achieved global stardom on their own terms. Morphing from chiming folk rock to mandolin-driven radio pop to singalong stadium anthems, their outsider status remained intact, their collaborative band identity solid. In every aspect of their journey, the band created an alt-rock template that inspired both artists and legions of fans worldwide.

## Melodic, Introspective Alt Rock

R.E.M. burst from early ‘80s Athens, GA, with a distinctive mix of jangle-pop guitar, propulsive rhythms, intriguing, inscrutable vocals, and a renowned live show. Evolving into a ‘90s and ‘00s arena act, they added synth, fuzz guitar, power ballads and anthems aplenty, remaining both accessible and slyly innovative.

From the Museum

## Rhinestoned R.E.M.

Bassist Mike Mills first donned a rhinestoned “Nudie suit” in 1994 during R.E.M.’s Monster tour. He then commissioned a series of lavish ensembles from foremost Western designer Manuel (previously Nudie’s head designer), who created this jacket (with matching pants).

“When you put one of these suits on,” said Mills, “you become a different person, but I tend to be that when I walk out onstage anyway.”

## As R.E.M. ascended from scrappy college rock beginnings to arenas, they achieved global stardom on their own terms. Morphing from chiming folk rock to mandolin-driven radio pop to singalong stadium anthems, their outsider status remained intact, their collaborative band identity solid. In every aspect of their journey, the band created an alt-rock template that inspired both artists and legions of fans worldwide.

Signature Sound

## Melodic, Introspective Alt Rock

R.E.M. burst from early ‘80s Athens, GA, with a distinctive mix of jangle-pop guitar, propulsive rhythms, intriguing, inscrutable vocals, and a renowned live show. ## Inductee Eddie Van Halen forever changed the vocabulary of the electric guitar. With blistering speed, control, and melodic feel, he perfected the art of shredding, unleashing two-handed finger tapping, dramatic whammy-bar moves, and other astonishing never-before-seen techniques. Innovative, like his hero Les Paul, Eddie reimagined the sonic possibilities of the guitar and became an inspiration for an entire generation of musicians who worshiped his sound and style. His band Van Halen kicked the American hard rock scene into high gear in the late Seventies, became rock heroes on MTV in the Eighties, and gave rise to a steady stream of shredders and trailblazers ever since.

## Inductee Eddie Van Halen forever changed the vocabulary of the electric guitar. With blistering speed, control, and melodic feel, he perfected the art of shredding, unleashing two-handed finger tapping, dramatic whammy-bar moves, and other astonishing never-before-seen techniques. Innovative, like his hero Les Paul, Eddie reimagined the sonic possibilities of the guitar and became an inspiration for an entire generation of musicians who worshiped his sound and style. His band Van Halen kicked the American hard rock scene into high gear in the late Seventies, became rock heroes on MTV in the Eighties, and gave rise to a steady stream of shredders and trailblazers ever since.

# Van Halen

![Image 2: An image of Van Halen](https://www.billboard.com/wp-content/themes/vip/pmc-billboard-2021/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif)

Helmed by the flamboyant, five-octave David Lee Roth and fueled by dynamite lead guitarist Eddie Van Halen, Van Halen set a new bar for heavy rock with 1978's "Runnin' with the Devil," their fiery instrumental "Eruption" and synth-pop crossovers like 1983's "Jump" and "Panama." The band was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2007.

# Van Halen

![Image 2: An image of Van Halen](https://www.billboard.com/wp-content/themes/vip/pmc-billboard-2021/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif)

Helmed by the flamboyant, five-octave David Lee Roth and fueled by dynamite lead guitarist Eddie Van Halen, Van Halen set a new bar for heavy rock with 1978's "Runnin' with the Devil," their fiery instrumental "Eruption" and synth-pop crossovers like 1983's "Jump" and "Panama." The band was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2007.

"**Jump**" is a song by American [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music") band [Van Halen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_Halen "Van Halen"). It was released in December 1983 as the lead single of their sixth studio album, _[1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984\_(Van\_Halen\_album) "1984 (Van Halen album)")_. It is Van Halen's most successful single, reaching number 1 on the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-1) The song differs from earlier Van Halen songs in that it is driven by a [keyboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_keyboard "Electronic keyboard") riff, although the song does contain a [guitar solo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guitar_solo "Guitar solo"). [David Lee Roth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Lee_Roth "David Lee Roth") dedicated the song to martial artist [Benny "The Jet" Urquidez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benny_Urquidez "Benny Urquidez"), of whom he was a student.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-Christe2009-2) In 2021, _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ ranked "Jump" at number 177 on its updated list of the "[500 Greatest Songs of All Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone's_500_Greatest_Songs_of_All_Time "Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Songs of All Time")".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-3)

"Jump" was one of the few Van Halen songs originally recorded by Roth that [Sammy Hagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sammy_Hagar "Sammy Hagar") would perform live during his tenures with the band.

## Writing and composition

The synth line was written circa 1981 by [Eddie Van Halen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Van_Halen "Eddie Van Halen"), but it was rejected by the other members of the band. In 1983, producer [Ted Templeman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Templeman "Ted Templeman") asked Roth to listen to the unused song idea. Riding around in the back of his 1951 [Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_(automobile) "Mercury (automobile)"), with band roadie Larry Hostler driving, Roth listened repeatedly to the tune. To come up with a lyric for it, he remembered seeing a TV news report the night before about a suicidal [jumper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jumper_(person) "Jumper (person)"). Roth thought that one of the onlookers at such an event would inevitably yell "go ahead and jump". Roth bounced this suggestion off Hostler who agreed it was good; however, instead of describing a potential suicide, the lyrics were written as an invitation to action, life and love. Roth later told [_Musician_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musician_(magazine) "Musician (magazine)") magazine that Hostler was "probably the most responsible for how it came out."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-4) The song is set in the key of [C major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C_major "C major"), with the guitar solo in the key of [B♭ minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B-flat_minor "B-flat minor"). "Jump" has a moderate [common time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_time "Common time")[tempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempo "Tempo") of 129 beats per minute.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-5)

Ted Templeman recalls that "Jump" was recorded at Eddie Van Halen's newly constructed home studio. "Engineer [Donn Landee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donn_Landee "Donn Landee") and Ed put the track down alone in the middle of the night. We recut it once in one take for sonic reasons. Dave wrote the lyrics that afternoon in the backseat of his Mercury convertible. We finished all vocals that afternoon and mixed it that evening."[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-6)

The keyboard part was performed on an [Oberheim OB-Xa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberheim_OB-Xa "Oberheim OB-Xa").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-7) Live performances began with Eddie's [synthesizer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthesizer "Synthesizer") solo "1984". During the reunion tour with Roth, the two songs were used for the band's encore.

According to [Daryl Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daryl_Hall "Daryl Hall") of [Hall & Oates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hall_&_Oates "Hall & Oates"), "[Eddie] Van Halen told me that he copied the synth part from '[Kiss on My List](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss_on_My_List "Kiss on My List")' and used it in 'Jump.' I don't have a problem with that at all."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-8)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6a/Van_Halen_-_Jump_2007-11-10.jpg/250px-Van_Halen_-_Jump_2007-11-10.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Van_Halen_-_Jump_2007-11-10.jpg)

Van Halen performs "Jump", November 10, 2007.

Musically, the song was a departure from the band's original style,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-9) embracing more of a popular and radio-friendly sound. "Jump" has been described as a "[synth-rocker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth-rock "Synth-rock")",[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-10) as a combination of hard rock and [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_music "Popular music"),[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-11) as exemplifying [pop rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_rock "Pop rock") of the 1980s, built on a classic [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music") foundation of repeated bass notes and having standard rock instrumentation,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-12) and as "a true rock masterpiece."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-Sumrall1994-13) The song has been also described as a [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_metal "Pop metal")/[glam metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glam_metal "Glam metal") anthem.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-vulture-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-18)

## Music video

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/4/45/David_Jumping.png/250px-David_Jumping.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:David_Jumping.png)

[David Lee Roth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Lee_Roth "David Lee Roth") seen jumping.

The music video for "Jump" was directed by [Pete Angelus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_Angelus "Pete Angelus") and [David Lee Roth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Lee_Roth "David Lee Roth"). It is a straightforward performance clip. It was nominated for three [MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award "MTV Video Music Award"), and won "Best Stage Performance" for the video. The audio mix of the song in video version has an extra "Ah oh oh!" yell from Roth before the last chorus.

In the 2011 book _MTV Ruled the World: The Early Years of Music Video_ by Greg Prato, Angelus discussed the video:

> "Jump" really was just about personality, really. It was a very simple video. We shot it for nothing. David wanted to incorporate his karate-flipping — that he loved so much — into the whole thing. The initial concept was just to film them in a very simple live setting, and let the personalities show through. We did it very quickly. Seriously, I think that we probably spent more money on pizza delivery than we did on the video itself. But that was the intention — make it a very intimate, personal feeling, with a very big band.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-MTV_Ruled_the_World-19)

## Sporting anthem

Since December 1986, before every home game at the [Stade Vélodrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_V%C3%A9lodrome "Stade Vélodrome"), [Olympique de Marseille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympique_de_Marseille "Olympique de Marseille") football players enter to Van Halen's song.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-20)

As part of the [goal celebrations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goal_celebration "Goal celebration") it is also played every time [A.C. Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.C._Milan "A.C. Milan") scores a goal at their home ground [San Siro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Siro "San Siro").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-21)

The song is a staple at [Detroit Pistons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Pistons "Detroit Pistons")[NBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") games whenever a jump ball is called.

The original [Winnipeg Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winnipeg_Jets_(1972%E2%80%9396) "Winnipeg Jets (1972–96)") of the [National Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Hockey_League "National Hockey League") played "Jump" on the arena PA system as the team came onto the ice. They used the song until the team's departure for Phoenix after the 1995–96 season. On the team's [return in 2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winnipeg_Jets "Winnipeg Jets"), public outcry for use of the song initially was ignored, as the team's management company [True North Sports and Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/True_North_Sports_and_Entertainment "True North Sports and Entertainment") wished to create a break with the past, considering the previous Jets a different organization from the new Jets (the former [Atlanta Thrashers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Thrashers "Atlanta Thrashers")). However, in 2016 True North resumed the use of "Jump", this time as the team's [goal song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goal_song "Goal song") whenever the Jets score a goal at [Bell MTS Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bell_MTS_Place "Bell MTS Place").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-22)

"Jump" was the theme song for the introduction of [Chicago Cubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Cubs "Chicago Cubs") broadcasts on [WGN-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WGN-TV "WGN-TV") in 1984 and 1985, and was formerly what the team would run onto the field to before the top of the 1st inning.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-24)

## Reception

Upon its release, the UK publication _[Music Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music\_Week "Music Week")_ felt that "Jump" catered to American sensibilities and characterized the song as "synthesizer pomp rock" with a "polite" vocal delivery from Roth.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-25) "Jump" was ranked number 15 on [VH1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VH1 "VH1")'s 100 Greatest Songs of the 1980s. The song was listed by [The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame_and_Museum "The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and Museum") as one of the "500 Songs that Shaped Rock and Roll."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-26) Chuck Klosterman of [Vulture.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulture.com "Vulture.com") ranked it the 16th-best Van Halen song, calling it "an articulation of unadulterated joy and the unprecedented power of six rudimentary keyboard chords arranged in the best possible sequence."[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-vulture-15) Ahead of the [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics"), the song was voted as the favourite sporting anthem, in a poll of members of [PRS for Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PRS_for_Music "PRS for Music").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-27)

## Appearances in film and television

The song was used in the soundtrack of the 2015 [biopic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biopic "Biopic")_[Eddie the Eagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie\_the\_Eagle\_(film) "Eddie the Eagle (film)")_, being described by Blake Goble of [Consequence of Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consequence_of_Sound "Consequence of Sound") as "the most on-the-nose use of Van Halen's 'Jump' ever committed to celluloid".[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-28) "Jump" appears in the 2018 science fiction film _[Ready Player One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ready\_Player\_One\_(film) "Ready Player One (film)")_. The song was used in the opening credits of the film and in the trailer for the film,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-30) and considered an "inspired choice" by Joe Reid of [Decider.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decider.com "Decider.com").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-31)

The song was featured by [McDonald's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonald's "McDonald's"), in their [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom") 2023 Christmas television commercial, titled _Fancy a McDonald's Christmas_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-33)

The song is heard in a scene of the 2005 film _[Herbie: Fully Loaded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbie:\_Fully\_Loaded "Herbie: Fully Loaded")_ where the titular character competes in a demolition derby.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Awards and nominations

"Jump" was nominated at the 27th Annual Grammy Awards (1984) in the "Best Rock Performance By a Duo or Group with Vocal" category, losing to _[Purple Rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purple\_Rain\_(album) "Purple Rain (album)")_ by [Prince & The Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_(musician) "Prince (musician)").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-34)

## Armin van Buuren remix

Dutch DJ [Armin van Buuren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armin_van_Buuren "Armin van Buuren") debuted his own private remix of "Jump" at the 2019 Miami [Ultra Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultra_Music_Festival "Ultra Music Festival") with David Lee Roth on stage.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-35) This remix was released through [Big Beat Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Beat_Records_(American_record_label) "Big Beat Records (American record label)") on May 17, 2019.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-36)

"Live: Jump" was released as a single in 1993. The performance was recorded at the [Selland Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selland_Arena "Selland Arena") in [Fresno, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fresno,_California "Fresno, California"), in May 1992, during the [For Unlawful Carnal Knowledge Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Unlawful_Carnal_Knowledge_Tour "For Unlawful Carnal Knowledge Tour"). "Jump" and the B-side, "[Love Walks In](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_Walks_In "Love Walks In")", are the same versions that appear on the album _[Live: Right Here, Right Now](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live:\_Right\_Here,\_Right\_Now "Live: Right Here, Right Now")_. On the [compact disc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compact_disc "Compact disc") release of the single, "[Mine All Mine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OU812 "OU812")" and "[Eagles Fly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eagles_Fly "Eagles Fly")" are previously unreleased live versions. All songs were produced by Van Halen and [Andy Johns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Johns "Andy Johns"), except "Mine All Mine", which was produced by Van Halen and [Donn Landee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donn_Landee "Donn Landee").[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-74)

"**Jump**" is a song by American [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music") band [Van Halen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_Halen "Van Halen"). It was released in December 1983 as the lead single of their sixth studio album, _[1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984\_(Van\_Halen\_album) "1984 (Van Halen album)")_. It is Van Halen's most successful single, reaching number 1 on the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-1) The song differs from earlier Van Halen songs in that it is driven by a [keyboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_keyboard "Electronic keyboard") riff, although the song does contain a [guitar solo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guitar_solo "Guitar solo"). [David Lee Roth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Lee_Roth "David Lee Roth") dedicated the song to martial artist [Benny "The Jet" Urquidez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benny_Urquidez "Benny Urquidez"), of whom he was a student.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-Christe2009-2) In 2021, _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ ranked "Jump" at number 177 on its updated list of the "[500 Greatest Songs of All Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone's_500_Greatest_Songs_of_All_Time "Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Songs of All Time")".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-3)

"Jump" was one of the few Van Halen songs originally recorded by Roth that [Sammy Hagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sammy_Hagar "Sammy Hagar") would perform live during his tenures with the band.

## Writing and composition

The synth line was written circa 1981 by [Eddie Van Halen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Van_Halen "Eddie Van Halen"), but it was rejected by the other members of the band. In 1983, producer [Ted Templeman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Templeman "Ted Templeman") asked Roth to listen to the unused song idea. Riding around in the back of his 1951 [Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_(automobile) "Mercury (automobile)"), with band roadie Larry Hostler driving, Roth listened repeatedly to the tune. To come up with a lyric for it, he remembered seeing a TV news report the night before about a suicidal [jumper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jumper_(person) "Jumper (person)"). Roth thought that one of the onlookers at such an event would inevitably yell "go ahead and jump". Roth bounced this suggestion off Hostler who agreed it was good; however, instead of describing a potential suicide, the lyrics were written as an invitation to action, life and love. Roth later told [_Musician_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musician_(magazine) "Musician (magazine)") magazine that Hostler was "probably the most responsible for how it came out."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-4) The song is set in the key of [C major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C_major "C major"), with the guitar solo in the key of [B♭ minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B-flat_minor "B-flat minor"). "Jump" has a moderate [common time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_time "Common time")[tempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempo "Tempo") of 129 beats per minute.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-5)

Ted Templeman recalls that "Jump" was recorded at Eddie Van Halen's newly constructed home studio. "Engineer [Donn Landee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donn_Landee "Donn Landee") and Ed put the track down alone in the middle of the night. We recut it once in one take for sonic reasons. Dave wrote the lyrics that afternoon in the backseat of his Mercury convertible. We finished all vocals that afternoon and mixed it that evening."[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-6)

The keyboard part was performed on an [Oberheim OB-Xa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberheim_OB-Xa "Oberheim OB-Xa").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-7) Live performances began with Eddie's [synthesizer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthesizer "Synthesizer") solo "1984". During the reunion tour with Roth, the two songs were used for the band's encore.

According to [Daryl Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daryl_Hall "Daryl Hall") of [Hall & Oates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hall_&_Oates "Hall & Oates"), "[Eddie] Van Halen told me that he copied the synth part from '[Kiss on My List](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss_on_My_List "Kiss on My List")' and used it in 'Jump.' I don't have a problem with that at all."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-8)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6a/Van_Halen_-_Jump_2007-11-10.jpg/250px-Van_Halen_-_Jump_2007-11-10.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Van_Halen_-_Jump_2007-11-10.jpg)

Van Halen performs "Jump", November 10, 2007.

Musically, the song was a departure from the band's original style,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-9) embracing more of a popular and radio-friendly sound. "Jump" has been described as a "[synth-rocker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth-rock "Synth-rock")",[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-10) as a combination of hard rock and [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_music "Popular music"),[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-11) as exemplifying [pop rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_rock "Pop rock") of the 1980s, built on a classic [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music") foundation of repeated bass notes and having standard rock instrumentation,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-12) and as "a true rock masterpiece."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-Sumrall1994-13) The song has been also described as a [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_metal "Pop metal")/[glam metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glam_metal "Glam metal") anthem.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-vulture-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-18)

## Music video

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/4/45/David_Jumping.png/250px-David_Jumping.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:David_Jumping.png)

[David Lee Roth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Lee_Roth "David Lee Roth") seen jumping.

The music video for "Jump" was directed by [Pete Angelus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_Angelus "Pete Angelus") and [David Lee Roth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Lee_Roth "David Lee Roth"). It is a straightforward performance clip. It was nominated for three [MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award "MTV Video Music Award"), and won "Best Stage Performance" for the video. The audio mix of the song in video version has an extra "Ah oh oh!" yell from Roth before the last chorus.

In the 2011 book _MTV Ruled the World: The Early Years of Music Video_ by Greg Prato, Angelus discussed the video:

> "Jump" really was just about personality, really. It was a very simple video. We shot it for nothing. David wanted to incorporate his karate-flipping — that he loved so much — into the whole thing. The initial concept was just to film them in a very simple live setting, and let the personalities show through. We did it very quickly. Seriously, I think that we probably spent more money on pizza delivery than we did on the video itself. But that was the intention — make it a very intimate, personal feeling, with a very big band.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-MTV_Ruled_the_World-19)

## Sporting anthem

Since December 1986, before every home game at the [Stade Vélodrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_V%C3%A9lodrome "Stade Vélodrome"), [Olympique de Marseille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympique_de_Marseille "Olympique de Marseille") football players enter to Van Halen's song.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-20)

As part of the [goal celebrations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goal_celebration "Goal celebration") it is also played every time [A.C. Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.C._Milan "A.C. Milan") scores a goal at their home ground [San Siro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Siro "San Siro").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-21)

The song is a staple at [Detroit Pistons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Pistons "Detroit Pistons")[NBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") games whenever a jump ball is called.

The original [Winnipeg Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winnipeg_Jets_(1972%E2%80%9396) "Winnipeg Jets (1972–96)") of the [National Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Hockey_League "National Hockey League") played "Jump" on the arena PA system as the team came onto the ice. They used the song until the team's departure for Phoenix after the 1995–96 season. On the team's [return in 2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winnipeg_Jets "Winnipeg Jets"), public outcry for use of the song initially was ignored, as the team's management company [True North Sports and Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/True_North_Sports_and_Entertainment "True North Sports and Entertainment") wished to create a break with the past, considering the previous Jets a different organization from the new Jets (the former [Atlanta Thrashers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Thrashers "Atlanta Thrashers")). However, in 2016 True North resumed the use of "Jump", this time as the team's [goal song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goal_song "Goal song") whenever the Jets score a goal at [Bell MTS Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bell_MTS_Place "Bell MTS Place").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-22)

"Jump" was the theme song for the introduction of [Chicago Cubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Cubs "Chicago Cubs") broadcasts on [WGN-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WGN-TV "WGN-TV") in 1984 and 1985, and was formerly what the team would run onto the field to before the top of the 1st inning.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-24)

## Reception

Upon its release, the UK publication _[Music Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music\_Week "Music Week")_ felt that "Jump" catered to American sensibilities and characterized the song as "synthesizer pomp rock" with a "polite" vocal delivery from Roth.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-25) "Jump" was ranked number 15 on [VH1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VH1 "VH1")'s 100 Greatest Songs of the 1980s. The song was listed by [The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame_and_Museum "The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and Museum") as one of the "500 Songs that Shaped Rock and Roll."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-26) Chuck Klosterman of [Vulture.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulture.com "Vulture.com") ranked it the 16th-best Van Halen song, calling it "an articulation of unadulterated joy and the unprecedented power of six rudimentary keyboard chords arranged in the best possible sequence."[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-vulture-15) Ahead of the [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics"), the song was voted as the favourite sporting anthem, in a poll of members of [PRS for Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PRS_for_Music "PRS for Music").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-27)

## Appearances in film and television

The song was used in the soundtrack of the 2015 [biopic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biopic "Biopic")_[Eddie the Eagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie\_the\_Eagle\_(film) "Eddie the Eagle (film)")_, being described by Blake Goble of [Consequence of Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consequence_of_Sound "Consequence of Sound") as "the most on-the-nose use of Van Halen's 'Jump' ever committed to celluloid".[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-28) "Jump" appears in the 2018 science fiction film _[Ready Player One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ready\_Player\_One\_(film) "Ready Player One (film)")_. The song was used in the opening credits of the film and in the trailer for the film,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-30) and considered an "inspired choice" by Joe Reid of [Decider.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decider.com "Decider.com").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-31)

The song was featured by [McDonald's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonald's "McDonald's"), in their [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom") 2023 Christmas television commercial, titled _Fancy a McDonald's Christmas_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-33)

The song is heard in a scene of the 2005 film _[Herbie: Fully Loaded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbie:\_Fully\_Loaded "Herbie: Fully Loaded")_ where the titular character competes in a demolition derby.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Awards and nominations

"Jump" was nominated at the 27th Annual Grammy Awards (1984) in the "Best Rock Performance By a Duo or Group with Vocal" category, losing to _[Purple Rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purple\_Rain\_(album) "Purple Rain (album)")_ by [Prince & The Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_(musician) "Prince (musician)").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-34)

## Armin van Buuren remix

Dutch DJ [Armin van Buuren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armin_van_Buuren "Armin van Buuren") debuted his own private remix of "Jump" at the 2019 Miami [Ultra Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultra_Music_Festival "Ultra Music Festival") with David Lee Roth on stage.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-35) This remix was released through [Big Beat Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Beat_Records_(American_record_label) "Big Beat Records (American record label)") on May 17, 2019.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-36)

"Live: Jump" was released as a single in 1993. The performance was recorded at the [Selland Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selland_Arena "Selland Arena") in [Fresno, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fresno,_California "Fresno, California"), in May 1992, during the [For Unlawful Carnal Knowledge Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Unlawful_Carnal_Knowledge_Tour "For Unlawful Carnal Knowledge Tour"). "Jump" and the B-side, "[Love Walks In](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_Walks_In "Love Walks In")", are the same versions that appear on the album _[Live: Right Here, Right Now](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live:\_Right\_Here,\_Right\_Now "Live: Right Here, Right Now")_. On the [compact disc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compact_disc "Compact disc") release of the single, "[Mine All Mine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OU812 "OU812")" and "[Eagles Fly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eagles_Fly "Eagles Fly")" are previously unreleased live versions. All songs were produced by Van Halen and [Andy Johns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Johns "Andy Johns"), except "Mine All Mine", which was produced by Van Halen and [Donn Landee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donn_Landee "Donn Landee").[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_(Van_Halen_song)#cite_note-74)

The **Rock and Roll Hall of Fame** (**RRHOF**), also simply referred to as the **Rock Hall**, is a [museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum "Museum") and [hall of fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hall_of_fame "Hall of fame") located in [downtown Cleveland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Cleveland "Downtown Cleveland"), Ohio, United States, on the shore of [Lake Erie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Erie "Lake Erie"). The museum documents the history of [rock music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music") and the artists, producers, engineers, and other personnel who have influenced its development.

The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame Foundation was established on April 20, 1983, by [Ahmet Ertegun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmet_Ertegun "Ahmet Ertegun"), founder and chairman of [Atlantic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Records "Atlantic Records"). After a long search for the right city, Cleveland was chosen in 1986 as the Hall of Fame's permanent home. Architect [I. M. Pei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I._M._Pei "I. M. Pei") designed the new museum, and it was dedicated on September 1, 1995.

## Foundation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Foundation")]

The RRHOF Foundation was established in 1983 by [Ahmet Ertegun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmet_Ertegun "Ahmet Ertegun"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-2) who assembled a team that included publisher of _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ magazine [Jann Wenner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jann_Wenner "Jann Wenner"), record executives [Seymour Stein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seymour_Stein "Seymour Stein"), [Bob Krasnow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Krasnow "Bob Krasnow"), and Noreen Woods, and attorneys [Allen Grubman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allen_Grubman "Allen Grubman") and Suzan Evans.

The Foundation began inducting artists in 1986, but the Hall of Fame still had no home. The search committee considered several cities, including [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia") (home to rock pioneer [Bill Haley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Haley "Bill Haley") and _[American Bandstand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Bandstand "American Bandstand")_); [Memphis, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis,_Tennessee "Memphis, Tennessee") (home of [Sun Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Studio "Sun Studio") and [Stax Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stax_Records "Stax Records")); [Detroit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit "Detroit") (home of [Motown Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motown_Records "Motown Records")); [Cincinnati, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati,_Ohio "Cincinnati, Ohio") (home of [King Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Records_(United_States) "King Records (United States)")); New York City; and Cleveland.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-Tribune_86-3)

Cleveland lobbied for the museum, with civic leaders in Cleveland pledging $65 million in public money to fund the construction, and citing that [WJW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WKNR "WKNR") disc jockey [Alan Freed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Freed "Alan Freed") both coined the term "[rock and roll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_roll "Rock and roll")" and heavily promoted the new genre, and that Cleveland was the location of Freed's [Moondog Coronation Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moondog_Coronation_Ball "Moondog Coronation Ball"), which is often credited as the first major rock and roll concert. Freed was also a member of the hall of fame's inaugural class of inductees in 1986.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-4) In addition, Cleveland cited radio station [WMMS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WMMS "WMMS"), which played a key role in breaking several major acts in the U.S. during the 1970s and 1980s, including [David Bowie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Bowie "David Bowie"), who began his first U.S. tour in the city, [Bruce Springsteen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Springsteen "Bruce Springsteen"), [Roxy Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roxy_Music "Roxy Music"), and [Rush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rush_(band) "Rush (band)"), among many others.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-5)

During early discussions on where to build the Hall of Fame and Museum, the Foundation's board considered a site along the Cuyahoga River in downtown Cleveland. Ultimately, the chosen location was along East Ninth Street in downtown by Lake Erie, east of [Cleveland Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Stadium "Cleveland Stadium"). At one point in the planning phase, when a financing gap existed, planners proposed locating the Rock Hall in the then-vacant May Company Building but finally decided to commission architect I. M. Pei to design a new building. Initial CEO [Larry R. Thompson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_R._Thompson "Larry R. Thompson") facilitated I. M. Pei in designs for the site. Pei came up with the idea of a tower with a glass pyramid protruding from it. Pei initially planned the tower to be 200 feet (61 m) high, but was forced to reduce it to 162 feet (49 m) due to the structure's proximity to [Burke Lakefront Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burke_Lakefront_Airport "Burke Lakefront Airport"). The building's base is approximately 150,000 square feet (14,000 m 2).

## Building

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Building")]

The [groundbreaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groundbreaking "Groundbreaking") ceremony for the building took place on June 7, 1993, with [Pete Townshend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_Townshend "Pete Townshend"), [Chuck Berry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Berry "Chuck Berry"), and [Billy Joel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Joel "Billy Joel") in attendance.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-6)

The museum was dedicated on September 1, 1995, with the ribbon being cut by an ensemble that included [Yoko Ono](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoko_Ono "Yoko Ono") and [Little Richard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Richard "Little Richard"), before a crowd of more than 10,000 people. The following night, an all-star concert was held at Cleveland Stadium[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-7) and featured Chuck Berry, [Bob Dylan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Dylan "Bob Dylan"), [Al Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Green "Al Green"), [Jerry Lee Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Lee_Lewis "Jerry Lee Lewis"), [Aretha Franklin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aretha_Franklin "Aretha Franklin"), [Bruce Springsteen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Springsteen "Bruce Springsteen"), [Iggy Pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iggy_Pop "Iggy Pop"), [John Fogerty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Fogerty "John Fogerty"), [John Mellencamp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Mellencamp "John Mellencamp"), and many others.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-HOF_Timeline-8)

In addition to the Hall of Fame inductees, the museum documents the entire history of rock and roll, regardless of induction status. Hall of Fame inductees are honored in a special exhibit located in a wing that juts out over Lake Erie.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-HOF_Timeline-8) The exhibit space and inaugural exhibits were designed by [Bruce Burdick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Burdick "Bruce Burdick")'s San Francisco design firm The Burdick Group.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-9)

Since 1986, the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame has selected new inductees. The formal induction ceremony has been held in New York City 28 times (1986–1992, 1994–1996, 1998–2008, 2010–2011, 2014, 2016, 2017, 2019, and 2023); four times in Los Angeles (1993, 2013, 2022, and 2025); and seven times in the hall of fame's home in Cleveland (1997, 2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, and 2024).

The 2009 and 2012 induction weeks were made possible by a [public–private partnership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public%E2%80%93private_partnership "Public–private partnership") between the City of Cleveland; the State of [Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio "Ohio"); the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame; and local foundations, corporations, civic organizations, and individuals. Collectively, these entities invested $5.8 million in 2009 and $7.9 million in 2012 to produce a week of events, including free concerts, a gospel celebration, exhibition openings, free admission to the museum, and induction ceremonies at Public Hall.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-10)

Millions viewed the television broadcast of the Cleveland inductions, and tens of thousands traveled to Ohio during induction week to participate in the events. The economic impact of the 2009 induction week activities was more than $13 million, and it provided an additional $20 million in media exposure for the region. The 2012 induction week yielded similar results.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-11)

In 2020, the Rock Hall announced plans to renovate and expand its footprint by a third. The architecture firm PAU, founded by Vishaan Chakrabarti, will lead the project.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-12)

### Layout

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Layout")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8a/North_Coast.jpg/960px-North_Coast.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:North_Coast.jpg "The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame (left) sits on the Lake Erie shore next to the Great Lakes Science Center (right) in Cleveland's North Coast Harbor.")

[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:North_Coast.jpg "File:North Coast.jpg")

The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame (left) sits on the [Lake Erie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Erie "Lake Erie") shore next to the [Great Lakes Science Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Lakes_Science_Center "Great Lakes Science Center") (right) in Cleveland's [North Coast Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Coast_Harbor "North Coast Harbor").

The building contains seven levels. On the lower level is the Ahmet M. Ertegun Exhibition Hall, the museum's main gallery, which includes exhibits on the roots of rock and roll ([gospel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gospel_music "Gospel music"), [blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blues "Blues"), [rhythm & blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythm_&_blues "Rhythm & blues") and [folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_music "Folk music"), [country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music"), and [bluegrass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bluegrass_music "Bluegrass music")). It also features exhibits on cities that have had a major impact on rock and roll: [Memphis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis,_Tennessee "Memphis, Tennessee"), [Detroit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit "Detroit"), [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool "Liverpool"), [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco"), [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"), and [Seattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle "Seattle"). There are exhibits about [soul music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_music "Soul music"), the Fifties, [Sun Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Records "Sun Records"), [hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop "Hip-hop"), Cleveland's rock and roll legacy, the music of the Midwest, rock and roll radio and dee-jays, and the many protests against rock and roll. This gallery also has exhibits that focus on individual artists, including [the Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles"), [the Rolling Stones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rolling_Stones "The Rolling Stones"), [Jimi Hendrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimi_Hendrix "Jimi Hendrix"), and others. Finally, the Ahmet M. Ertegun Exhibition Hall includes a theatre that features films on various subjects such as [American Bandstand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Bandstand "American Bandstand").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-13)

The first floor of the museum is the entrance level. It includes a café, a stage that the museum uses for various special performances and events throughout the year, and a section called "Backstage Stories". The second floor includes several interactive kiosks that feature programs on [one-hit wonders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One-hit_wonders "One-hit wonders") and the Songs That Shaped Rock and Roll. This level also includes a gallery with artifact-filled exhibits about [Les Paul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Les_Paul "Les Paul"), Alan Freed, [Sam Phillips](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Phillips_(record_producer) "Sam Phillips (record producer)"), and the evolution of audio technology.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-14)

Visitors enter the Hall of Fame section of the museum on the third floor. This section includes "The Power of Rock Experience", which includes one of [Jonathan Demme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Demme "Jonathan Demme")'s final works, a film shown in the Connor Theater. The film includes musical highlights from some of the Hall's induction ceremonies.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-15) Visitors exit the Hall of Fame section on the fourth floor. That level features the Foster Theater, a state-of-the-art 3-D theater that is used for special events and programs.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-17)

Finally, the top two levels of the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame feature large, temporary exhibits. Over the years, numerous exhibits have been installed on these two levels, including exhibits about [Elvis Presley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Presley "Elvis Presley"), [hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop "Hip-hop"), [the Supremes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Supremes "The Supremes"), [the Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Who "The Who"), [U2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U2 "U2"), [John Lennon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lennon "John Lennon"), [the Clash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Clash "The Clash"), the [Grateful Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grateful_Dead "Grateful Dead"), Bruce Springsteen, _Women Who Rock_, and the [Rolling Stones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stones "Rolling Stones").

### Architecture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Architecture")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b8/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame.jpg/250px-Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame.jpg)

The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, showing [Lake Erie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Erie "Lake Erie") in the foreground

Designed by [I. M. Pei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I._M._Pei "I. M. Pei") and structurally engineered by [Leslie E. Robertson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leslie_E._Robertson "Leslie E. Robertson") Associates, the building rises above the shores of [Lake Erie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Erie "Lake Erie"). It is a combination of geometric forms and cantilevered spaces that are anchored by a 162-foot (49 m) tower. The tower supports a dual-triangular-shaped glass "tent" that extends (at its base) onto a 65,000-square-foot (6,000 m 2) plaza that provides a main entry facade.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-18)

The building houses more than 55,000 square feet (5,100 m 2) of exhibition space, as well as administrative offices, a store, and a café.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-19)

"In designing this building," Pei said, "it was my intention to echo the energy of rock and roll. I have consciously used an architectural vocabulary that is bold and new, and I hope the building will become a dramatic landmark for the city of [Cleveland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland "Cleveland") and for fans of [rock and roll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_roll "Rock and roll") around the world."[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-20)

### New York City Annex

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: New York City Annex")]

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Rock-roll-annex-76-Mercer.jpg/250px-Rock-roll-annex-76-Mercer.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rock-roll-annex-76-Mercer.jpg)

The museum's New York City Annex (2008–2010) on [Mercer Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercer_Street_(Manhattan) "Mercer Street (Manhattan)") in [Soho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SoHo,_Manhattan "SoHo, Manhattan")

In 2006, the RRHOF partnered with three entertainment production companies to create a branch museum in New York City.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-Sisario-21) On November 18, 2008, the **Rock and Roll Hall of Fame Annex NYC** opened in [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan")'s [SoHo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SoHo,_Manhattan "SoHo, Manhattan") district.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-Sisario-21) Located at 76 [Mercer Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercer_Street_(Manhattan) "Mercer Street (Manhattan)") just west of [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_(Manhattan) "Broadway (Manhattan)"), the Annex occupied an underground space of 25,000 square feet (2,300 m 2).[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-Sisario-21) The branch museum operated in much the same way as its Cleveland parent, featuring archetypal display pieces like [Prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_(musician) "Prince (musician)")'s coat from _[Purple Rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purple\_Rain\_(film) "Purple Rain (film)")_, [David Byrne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Byrne "David Byrne")'s "big suit" from _[Stop Making Sense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stop\_Making\_Sense "Stop Making Sense")_, and [Elvis Presley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Presley "Elvis Presley")'s motorcycle jacket and Bible.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-Sisario-21) But from its start, the Annex also had a distinct [New York area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_area "New York area") focus that made plenty of space for big items like the phone booth from [CBGB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBGB "CBGB"), layered thick with band stickers over the decades; Bruce Springsteen's own [1957 Chevrolet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1957_Chevrolet "1957 Chevrolet"); a special gallery reserved for the city's musicians; and an intricate 26-foot (7.9 m) scale model of Manhattan highlighting sites of rock history.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-Sisario-21)

Jann Wenner served as chairman of the board of the Annex.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-Soeder-22) At its opening night gala, he inadvertently created a controversy after he told a reporter, "One of the small sad things is we didn't do it in New York in the first place."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-Soeder-22) He later expressed regret for his remark, which he said had been misconstrued and clarified that "I am absolutely delighted that the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and Museum is in Cleveland."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-Soeder-22)

The Annex closed on January 3, 2010, its quick demise reportedly due to the [2008 financial crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_financial_crisis "2008 financial crisis") and a subsequent downturn in the city's tourism.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-Durkin-23) The museum's final major exhibition was about [John Lennon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lennon "John Lennon") and his years in New York City.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-Durkin-23)

## Exhibits and features

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Exhibits and features")]

Since 1997, the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame has featured numerous temporary exhibits that range in size from major exhibits that fill the top two floors of the museum to smaller exhibits that are often installed in the main exhibition hall on the lower level.

The museum's first major exhibit opened on May 10, 1997. It was called _I Want to Take You Higher: The Psychedelic Era, 1965–1969_ and included memorabilia from numerous artists including [John Lennon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lennon "John Lennon"), [Eric Clapton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Clapton "Eric Clapton"), [John Sebastian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Sebastian "John Sebastian"), [Jefferson Airplane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_Airplane "Jefferson Airplane"), and [Janis Joplin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janis_Joplin "Janis Joplin"), as well as items related to the 1967 [Monterey Pop Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monterey_Pop_Festival "Monterey Pop Festival") and 1969's [Woodstock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodstock "Woodstock").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-24)

That exhibit was followed by _Elvis Is in the Building_, which ran from August 8, 1998, to September 5, 1999. This year-long tribute was the first exhibit devoted to a single artist: Elvis Presley, the "King of Rock and Roll" and the first inductee into the RRHOF in 1986. [Graceland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graceland "Graceland") supplied a significant selection of representative artifacts for this special tribute that spanned Presley's life and career.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-25) Next, the museum curated _Roots, Rhymes and Rage: The Hip-Hop Story_,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-26) which was the first major museum exhibit to focus on hip-hop. It ran from November 11, 1999, to August 6, 2000. It was followed by _Rock Style_, an exhibit that focused on both rock and roll and fashion. It featured clothing from [Buddy Holly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddy_Holly "Buddy Holly") to [Alice Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice_Cooper "Alice Cooper"), [Ray Charles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Charles "Ray Charles") to [David Bowie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Bowie "David Bowie"), and [Smokey Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smokey_Robinson "Smokey Robinson") to [Sly Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sly_Stone "Sly Stone"). After it closed in Cleveland, _Rock Style_ traveled to other museums in the U.S.

Other temporary exhibits have included _Lennon: His Life and Work_, which ran from October 20, 2000, to January 1, 2003, followed by _In the Name of Love: Two Decades of [U2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U2 "U2")_ and _Reflections: The [Mary Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary\_Wilson\_(singer) "Mary Wilson (singer)") Supreme Legacy Collection_. A major exhibition titled _Louder than Words: Rock, Power, Politics_ was on display during the [2016 Republican National Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Republican_National_Convention "2016 Republican National Convention") in Cleveland.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-28)

Other large temporary exhibits have focused on [the Clash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Clash "The Clash") (_Revolution Rock: The Story of the Clash_), [the Doors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Doors "The Doors") (_Break on Through: The Lasting Legacy of the Doors_), [the Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Who "The Who")'s _[Tommy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy\_(The\_Who\_album) "Tommy (The Who album)")_ (_Tommy: The Amazing Journey_), and [Bruce Springsteen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Springsteen "Bruce Springsteen") (_From Asbury Park to the Promised Land: The Life and Music of Bruce Springsteen_). Another thematic temporary exhibit focused on the role of women in rock and roll (_Women Who Rock: Vision, Passion, Power_). Many of these exhibits travel to other museums after closing in Cleveland. A major temporary exhibit in 2017 told the story and impact of _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ magazine.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-29)

The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame also curates many smaller temporary exhibits. Over the years, these exhibits have focused on such topics as the [Vans Warped Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vans_Warped_Tour "Vans Warped Tour"), [the Concert for Bangladesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Concert_for_Bangladesh "The Concert for Bangladesh"), Woodstock's 40th and 50th anniversaries, [Austin City Limits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_City_Limits "Austin City Limits"), the [Monterey International Pop Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monterey_International_Pop_Festival "Monterey International Pop Festival"), [Roy Orbison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Orbison "Roy Orbison"), Motown's 50th anniversary, [Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Petty_and_the_Heartbreakers "Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers"), [Marty Stuart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marty_Stuart "Marty Stuart"), [Paul Simon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Simon "Paul Simon"), [Graham Nash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graham_Nash "Graham Nash"), [John Mellencamp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Mellencamp "John Mellencamp"), and [Geddy Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geddy_Lee "Geddy Lee")'s basses.

The museum also devotes exhibits to photography and artwork related to rock and roll. Among the photographers whose work has been featured at the Hall of Fame are [George Kalinsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Kalinsky "George Kalinsky"), [Alfred Wertheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Wertheimer "Alfred Wertheimer"), Tommy Edwards, Kevin Mazur, Janet Macoska, [Lynn Goldsmith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lynn_Goldsmith "Lynn Goldsmith"), [Linda McCartney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linda_McCartney "Linda McCartney"), [Mike McCartney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_McCartney "Mike McCartney"), Robert Alford,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-30) and George Shuba. The museum also featured the artwork of Philip Burke in one of its temporary exhibits, and a later exhibit featured Herb Ritts.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-31)

The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and Museum produces numerous public programs, including concerts, interviews, lectures, film screenings, and other events that help tell the story of rock and roll. Every February, the museum celebrates [Black History Month](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_History_Month "Black History Month") by hosting concerts, film screenings, and lectures that illustrate the important role African-Americans have played in the history of rock and roll.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-32)

Another program is the Hall of Fame Series. This series began in April 1996 and features interviews with Hall of Fame inductees in rare and intimate settings, most often in the Museum's Foster Theater. The interviews are usually followed by a question-and-answer session with the audience and, often, a performance by the inductee.

A similar program is the Legends Series, whose only real difference from the Hall of Fame Series program is that it features artists who have not yet been inducted into the Hall of Fame. [Peter Hook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Hook "Peter Hook") of [Joy Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joy_Division "Joy Division"), [Spinderella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spinderella "Spinderella") of [Salt n Pepa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_n_Pepa "Salt n Pepa"), [Tommy James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_James "Tommy James"), and [the Chi-Lites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Chi-Lites "The Chi-Lites") are among the artists who have participated in the Legends Series.

The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and Museum's most acclaimed program[_[according to whom?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Words\_to\_watch#Unsupported\_attributions "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Words to watch")_] is the annual American Music Masters series. Each year, the museum celebrates one of the Hall's inductees with a week-long series of programs that includes interviews, film screenings, and, often, a special exhibit. The celebration ends with an all-star concert held at a Cleveland theater. The concerts include a diverse mix of artists—from Hall of Fame inductees to contemporary musicians.

The American Music Masters series began in 1996 with _Hard Travelin': The Life and Legacy of Pete Seeger_. ### List of "The Songs That Shaped Rock and Roll"

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: List of \"The Songs That Shaped Rock and Roll\"")]

Hall of Fame museum curator James Henke, along with "the museum's curatorial staff and numerous rock critics and music experts", created an unordered list of "500 Songs That Shaped Rock and Roll."[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-41) The list is part of a permanent exhibit at the museum, and was envisioned as part of the museum from its opening in 1995.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-42) It contains songs recorded from the [1920s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stagger_Lee_(song) "Stagger Lee (song)") through the 1990s. The oldest song on the list is "[Wabash Cannonball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wabash_Cannonball "Wabash Cannonball")" (in particular [Roy Acuff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Acuff "Roy Acuff")'s 1936 version), written c.1882 and credited to J. A. Roff.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-655_Songs-44) Since then, however, an additional 160 songs have been added, and the list is now simply referred to as "The Songs That Shaped Rock and Roll." The most recent songs on the list are [Gnarls Barkley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gnarls_Barkley "Gnarls Barkley")'s "[Crazy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crazy_(Gnarls_Barkley_song) "Crazy (Gnarls Barkley song)")" and [My Chemical Romance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Chemical_Romance "My Chemical Romance")'s "[Welcome to the Black Parade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welcome_to_the_Black_Parade "Welcome to the Black Parade")," which were both released in 2006. The Beatles and the Rolling Stones are the most represented on the 660-song list, with eight songs each.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-655_Songs-44)
